page: Microsoft Azure M128pds_v4 belongs to the Mpdsv4 memory-optimized virtual machine family. Powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1388.0 GB of total RAM. This configuration delivers an expansive memory density of 10.84 GB per core, accommodating workloads requiring substantial in-memory footprints without compute contention.

The instance includes 7560 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-bandwidth, low-latency scratch disk space alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. It contains no GPU hardware acceleration and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing physical resources strictly on general compute, memory allocation, and local I/O capacity.

By adopting ARM-based silicon, the M128pds_v4 yields high resource density and operational efficiency compared to traditional x86 alternatives, though it requires ARM-compatible software stacks. The massive memory allocation combined with substantial local NVMe storage makes this configuration appropriate for large in-memory databases, enterprise data warehousing, distributed caching clusters, and high-throughput transactional analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure M128pds_v4 is an enterprise-scale memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 architecture. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 1388.0 GB of RAM, offering approximately 10.84 GB of memory per core to support memory-heavy computing environments. Complementing its substantial memory footprint, the instance includes 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage along with support for Premium Storage tiers. No discrete GPU accelerators are attached. The architecture combines high core counts, large memory capacity, and fast local solid-state drives, trading x86 compatibility for the resource efficiency of ARM computing. Workloads that benefit most from this hardware profile include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise data analytics, memory-bound caching clusters, and high-throughput transactional processing systems.
